330: ## AUDIT — vibeweaver-audit plugin (Tier-0/1/2) ★ MANDATORY
331: 
332: The `vibeweaver-audit` plugin (installed beside vibeweaver-gate.js in
333: `~/.config/opencode/plugins/`) mechanically audits every session that loaded
334: the vibeweaver skill. It runs no LLM, needs no prompt, and requires ZERO
335: cooperation from the agent — it observes passively (message parts + tool
336: calls). Full architecture notes: this file's preface in the skill.
337: 
338: **What it checks (three-state OK / BAD / UNCERTAIN):**
339: - **Group A — on-disk artifacts:** verification_log has ≥1 `- iter` entry ·
340:   acceptance.md first line `> cap=5  stall=3×` · every cited media/screenshot
341:   exists >0 bytes · assert_artifacts.py actually runs and exits 0.
342: - **Group B — narration markers in your text:** `[Verification Gate]` ·
343:   `HARD-GATE-1: NO-TEST-NO-DONE` · `HARD-GATE-2: SCRIPT-ONLY` ·
344:   `[Covenant Recall]` · `[Memory Gate]` · `[Convergence]` · 8-column table
345:   header · `assert_artifacts.py: pass=N/fail=0` · `covenant_recall: pass` ·
346:   `memory_gate: pass`.
347: - **Group C — claim↔artifact cross-checks of the gate line (triage):**
348:   `Loop executed` ↔ iter entries · `Iterations` ↔ log count · `Media graded` ↔
349:   files on disk · `E2E depth` ↔ `tests/workflows/*.trace.log` · `TDD RED` ↔
350:   `- iter N FAIL:` · `Fresh-run` ↔ commit time vs log write · `Code review`
351:   ↔ dispatch/reason · script-only ↔ bash (raw `npm run build`/`vite`/`npm
352:   start`/`uvicorn`/`pkill -f` forbidden) · R1/R1b reads ↔ read tool calls ·
353:   verifier announcement · COV-9 entry · HARD-GATE-1/2 values.
354: 
355: **Report:** written to `tests/gate_audit.md` at session idle (refreshed at
356: every session idle, which fires after EVERY assistant turn). The FULL final
357: audit runs only when the session text contains the completion markers
358: (`[Verification Gate]` or the 8-column table header); in-progress turns get
359: the warn-only mid audit and never set BLOCKING (multi-turn tasks must not
360: deadlock). First line is the verdict:
361: ```
362: AUDIT: BAD=n UNCERTAIN=n escalate=true|false reasons=[BAD,UNCERTAIN,HIGH-RISK,SAMPLING] BLOCKING=yes|no
363: ```
364: - `BLOCKING=yes` latches RED at the project root (persisted per project root in
365:   `.vibeweaver/audit-state.json`, with the latching session's ID embedded in the
366:   latch value) and the next
367:   non-test `write`/`edit` throws GATE-BLOCKED (`tool.execute.before`).
368:   **The latch is scoped to the session that earned it:**
369:   - The latching session stays blocked while it continues — self-correct:
370:     repair each `[BAD]` item (fix the evidence, append `- audit-fix: …` /
371:     `- audit-ruling: …` entries to `tests/verification_log.md`) and re-emit
372:     a corrected `[Verification Gate]` line; the audit re-runs at every idle
373:     and on every write. No human action is needed.
374:   - Session-scoped, D3 (2026-10-15): a FOREIGN session's writes never clear
375:     the latch (the old takeover release was a bypass). Releases: the latching
376:     session's OWN next task (new-task key below), the TTL (`redTtlHours`,
377:     default 24h), or legacy (pre session-scoping) state. `tests/` stays
378:     writable throughout. Every release is recorded — `redReleases` (bounded
379:     to 5), the app log, and the report's `## Stale RED releases` — never
380:     silently dropped.
381:   - **Same-session new-task key (2026-10-02, multi-wave DOC→CODE deadlock):**
382:     the first action of a new task is writing `tests/acceptance.md` (Step 1,
383:     `tests/` is writable under the latch) — an acceptance rewrite whose
384:     floor(mtime) is strictly AFTER the latch `ts` releases on the session's
385:     next gated write/idle, journaled `new-task` (an already-expired latch
386:     journals `ttl-expiry`; the dominant fact wins). Same-ms ties resolve to
387:     "no release"; a backward clock step is the remaining skew corner
388:     (fail-safe: stays blocked). The old wave's debt stays in
389:     `tests/gate_audit.md`; the new wave's completion claim re-checks
390:     everything (re-arm leg below).
391:   - **BAD-signature guard (no re-latch treadmill; r2 hardening):** a final
392:     audit scores the WHOLE buffer, so re-audits of an unchanged failure must
393:     not re-latch. Re-latch requires a genuinely new failure: the *session
394:     signature* (sorted BAD ids, keyed PER SESSION — root keys would amnesty
395:     a different session's first failure) or the *completion-marker count*
396:     (grows by one per NEW claim — a new claim re-arms even with an identical
397:     signature; same-claim re-audits stay suppressed). A live latch is never
398:     refreshed (TTL backstop stays real); a GREEN final clears the latch,
399:     signature and count. Boundaries: two claims >150KB apart can trim the
400:     earlier marker (head 20KB kept) — the count leg misses one re-arm, the
401:     signature leg still fires; quoted marker mentions count too — fail-closed,
402:     journaled. Pre-deploy latches carry no signature and may re-latch once
403:     before the guard records theirs — self-healing in one cycle.
404:   - Any `test`/`tests` directory in the project (top-level `tests/`,
405:     `dev/tests/`, `src/test/`, …) stays writable while RED, so the
406:     evidence-fix path can never deadlock.
407: - `escalate=true` → the Tier-2 contract below applies.
408: 
409: **Tier-2 escalation contract (escalate=true — YOUR obligation, NOT optional):**
410: 1. Read `tests/gate_audit.md` IN FULL: every `[BAD]` line names the broken
411:    artifact/claim; every `[UNCERTAIN]` line names what could not be verified
412:    mechanically, with a review packet (`<packet id="C9">...`) of the evidence.
413: 2. Dispatch a **fresh-brain reviewer** (opencode `task` tool, READ-ONLY,
414:    per §A4.9 verdict contract — Strengths · Critical/Important/Minor with
415:    file:line · Assessment) with ONLY: `tests/gate_audit.md` +
416:    `tests/acceptance.md` + `tests/verification_log.md` + the review packets.
417:    Ask it to answer, per packet: *did this step genuinely happen, on the
418:    evidence in the transcript/artifacts?*
419: 3. Fix Critical/Important findings; log every fix as
420:    `- audit-fix: <finding> | changed: <file>` in `tests/verification_log.md`
421:    (machine-recognizable prefix, same format discipline as `diagnosis:`).
422:    A false positive gets `- audit-ruling: <packet> — false positive, reason: …`
423:    — never silently delete an audit line.
424: 4. Re-run the audit (any write re-checks; or read gate_audit.md after the
425:    next write) until `BLOCKING=no`. `escalate` may persist on SAMPLING —
426:    that is by design (asymmetry rule: an all-green mechanical report is NOT
427:    a clearance; ~10% of sessions are escalated by hash regardless of
428:    verdicts to catch ritual compliance — reviewer cost is the price).
429: 
430: **Scope discipline:** sessions that never loaded the vibeweaver skill are
431: not audited (subagent reviewers, unrelated chats) — silent. Doc-only tasks
432: emit the gate line with `na`/`no` values; the audit accepts those claims at
433: face value (no artifact demanded). Disable per-run: `VIBEWEAVER_AUDIT=off`.
434: 
435: **Loop-guard (degenerate-generation watchdog):** the same text observation
436: channel also watches for runaway output, independent of the artifact audit.
437: Five shapes, detected the moment they emerge from the assistant text stream
438: (reasoning parts ride the same machinery in their own buffer and episode budget):
439: (a) an identical line-group repeating at the tail — period derived from the
440: data (any block period up to 640 lines within the 96KB tail window, i.e.
441: realistic code up to ~50 chars/line), multi-line groups at ≥3×; a single
442: repeated line needs ≥4× and punctuation-only separator lines are ignored
443: (identical banner/log lines ×3 are legitimate codegen); (b) a trailing run of
444: ≥12 bare tokens stepping +1 — integers (`1,2,…,179`) or bijective base-26
445: letters (`a,b,…,kf`); (c) line-sparse (no-newline) tails — a char-level
446: suffix period: the same ≥32-char string repeated ≥4× (with a letter/digit;
447: short sub-period streams are caught at their ≥32-char super-period), e.g. a
448: sentence streamed back-to-back with no line breaks; trailing whitespace/newline
449: noise is normalized at scan entry on every detector path, and a ≥256-char last
450: line enters the scan even under newline-rich context); (d) counter-bearing
451: line runs — ≥16 consecutive tail lines with identical non-digit shape whose
452: every digit run steps strictly +1 (`The backlog item {i} …` walls; strict +1
453: excludes timestamp logs and `page N of M`; a single trailing status line does
454: not mask the run); (e) punctuation-only walls — a punct-only suffix period
455: counts only once the wall's own trailing punctuation run is ≥2KB (a big
456: report ending in a short rule/banner and ASCII-art separators stay clean);
457: plus a visible-text-only ceiling: >256KB fires `runaway` (re-armed per 256KB;
458: `loopGuardTurnCeilingBytes`, min 64KB; reasoning excluded, independent 1MB
459: backstop `loopGuardReasoningCeilingBytes` (min 256KB); id-less hosts reset at
460: the user boundary — unseen-shape backstop). Repeated JSX/HTML
461: elements ×3 and pure-punctuation runs stay clean by the same bar. On trigger
462: the plugin interrupts the session (v1 `session.abort` / v2
463: `session.interrupt({continue:false})`) and posts a corrective prompt naming
464: the pattern (restate the task in one line + the single next concrete step).
465: One intervention per degeneration episode (re-arms after clean text or a NEW
466: assistant turn — fresh-turn re-degeneration gets its own intervention;
467: same-turn continuation never re-fires), budget 2 per session per
468: channel (further episodes are log-only, config
469: `loopGuardMaxInterventions` in `audit.json`). Near-misses excluded:
470: numbered lists with content (`1. step`) are not bare tokens;
471: a 2× repetition is below the bar. Disable per-run:
472: `VIBEWEAVER_LOOPGUARD=off`.
473: 
474: **C8 self-clearing rule:** a forbidden raw command (C8) flags only ONCE per
475: project root (command-hash dedup, persisted in `.vibeweaver/audit-state.json`
476: `c8Flagged`). Immutable session history can never pin a session in a
477: permanent RED latch — the latch clears on the next GREEN audit; every NEW
478: distinct forbidden command still flags. The dedup is persisted only by the
479: FINAL audit: a mid-phase warning never consumes the one-shot, so a forbidden
480: command run mid-task still latches when the completion audit lands.
481: 
482: **Config lives OUTSIDE the agent's write scope:** global only —
483: `~/.config/opencode/vibeweaver/audit.json` (overrides DEFAULTS:
484: `samplingRate` · `escOnUncertain` · `escOnHighRisk` · `forbiddenRaw`).
485: A project-local `.vibeweaver/audit.json` is DELIBERATELY IGNORED — the agent
486: can write it, and a model under prompt injection would use it to disable its
487: own auditor (the optimizer must never have write access to its own objective
488: function).
489: 
490: **Known boundaries (by design, not bugs):** the audit proves tokens, files
491: and orderings — never intent. `na`/`no` claims are accepted at face value;
492: A4.9 trigger classification rests on the model's self-assessment; process
493: compliance is not outcome correctness. Those are the reviewer's (and the
494: user's) judgments — the audit's job is to make the machine-checkable layer
495: honest. A truncated/aborted session's buffered text may be incomplete
496: (head/tail caps), so its final audit can latch RED on partial evidence —
497: that is the latch being conservative, and it is bounded precisely because
498: of this: it yields to the session's own next task (new-task key) or expires
499: with its TTL (D3: a FOREIGN session's writes never clear it); is fully
500: recorded; its re-audit cannot feed on an unchanged failure signature; and
501: the evidence path (tests/) stays writable so it can never dead-lock a fix.

247: ## A4.4.2 Physical Gate (plugin enforcement — do not fight it) ★
248: 
249: The `vibeweaver-gate` plugin (`~/.config/opencode/plugins/vibeweaver-gate.js`)
250: enforces §A4.4.1 mechanically. After every `write`/`edit`, when the project
251: is vibeweaver-active (has `tests/verification_log.md`), it runs
252: `tests/assert_artifacts.py` (trying `--existing` / `--backend-only`
253: variants) and **throws a GATE-BLOCKED error into the tool result** while
254: verification evidence is missing or falsified. Bash is deliberately NOT
255: gated (screenshots / server start must be free to produce evidence), and
256: non-vibeweaver projects are silent. **Known boundary (named, accepted):**
257: file mutations performed THROUGH bash (`sed -i`, `>`, editor scripts) bypass
258: both the gate and §A7.16 cue delivery — hooking bash command text costs more
259: false alarms than it catches. Mitigation is procedural, not mechanical: the
260: completion-time `assert_artifacts.py --final` run + the audit's B12
261: final-run check examine the resulting tree regardless of how it was edited.
262: 
263: - **Fail-closed (D4):** EVERY assert failure blocks (evidence and structure);
264:   only `WARN` lines stay advisory. "The check could not run" is itself a BLOCK
265:   (python3 missing, timeout, crash, placeholder/stub). A legacy prose-only
266:   copy fails closed too (upgrade from `scripts/`). `--json` prints
267:   `{ok, passes, fails:[{code,severity,detail}]}`.
268: - `session.idle` with a RED gate writes a `warn` entry to the opencode log
269:   (tripwire when the agent stops on a red gate).
270: - **Stall observer (stateful):** `.vibeweaver/state.json` (gitignore it)
271:   keeps the last ≤20 ops + the `iter N PASS` count; the SAME file edited 3×
272:   with no new PASS gets a `[GATE-WARNING]` stall note (§A4.10). Warnings only
273:   — never blocks (COV-7, machine-counted).
274: - Escape hatch: `VIBEWEAVER_GATE=off` disables the plugin.
275: - If `tests/assert_artifacts.py` does not exist yet, the plugin runs an
276:   inline evidence check and the GATE-BLOCKED message points to §A4.4.1.
277: - **Trust model:** laziness/drift, not hostile root — fake checker → pin
278:   (T2); protected evidence → lock (T2.5). `tests/` exempt.
279: - **Seal three-state (G1, W18)** — `tests/evidence_manifest.json` +
280:   `tests/test_baseline.json`, written ONLY by `scripts/evidence_seal.py`
281:   (SLSA/in-toto verdicts — "missing" is never rendered as "stale"):
282: 
283:   | state | condition | verdict |
284:   |---|---|---|
285:   | `no-seal` | neither file exists | WARN `evidence seal: none yet — run scripts/evidence_seal.py after the first green test run` (bootstrap; sealing is opt-in) |
286:   | `partial` | baseline only | C3 finding — a seal once existed; deleting the manifest clears nothing |
287:   | `tamper` | hash mismatch / sealed file gone | C3 finding `… (C3 tamper)` / `sealed evidence missing … (C3)` |
288:   | `stale` | code changed after sealing | C3 finding `sealed evidence is STALE (C3 freshness) …` |
289:   | `current` | seal matches the tree | silent |
290: 
291:   A C3 finding BLOCKs when the seal obligation is live, WARNs
292:   (`advisory until the first green - iter N PASS`) in the bootstrap window
293:   (no green PASS in the current task block — the wave's backup anchor makes
294:   old seals fresh-stale at wave start; W12's 30+ false banners). `--final`
295:   ALWAYS enforces (completion = the sealing moment); the cited-media rule
296:   (`cited media evidence is not sealed (C3)`) is unconditional; the green
297:   marker uses COV-1's `PASS\b` grammar.
298: - **`tests/` writes are never gated — either arg shape:** write/edit carry
299:   the target as `args.path` (canonical) or `args.filePath` (adapter); the
300:   exemption resolves both (symlink-safe normalize, EXACT first segment
301:   `tests/` · `test/` · `memory/`; nested `src/tests/` is not evidence).
302:   **Protected evidence (T2.5):** checker/acceptance/profile/debt/lock/
303:   gate_result are gated; the lock is written only by `scripts/evidence_lock.py`.
304: 
305: The GATE-BLOCKED message means **keep working — fix the evidence, then the
306: next write/edit re-checks automatically**. It is a completion gate, not an
307: execution stop.

313: Every stage of a task commits an artifact the NEXT stage reads; together they

315: it). Each artifact MUST name its upstream link, so the chain can be walked in
316: both directions:
317: 
318: - `tests/acceptance.md` ← its source (user request / design doc / incident).
319: - `tests/verification_log.md` ← criterion numbers per entry (A4.1 Step 4).

330: ## AUDIT — vibeweaver-audit plugin (Tier-0/1/2) ★ MANDATORY
331: 
332: The `vibeweaver-audit` plugin (installed beside vibeweaver-gate.js in
333: `~/.config/opencode/plugins/`) mechanically audits every session that loaded
334: the vibeweaver skill. It runs no LLM, needs no prompt, and requires ZERO
335: cooperation from the agent — it observes passively (message parts + tool
336: calls). Full architecture notes: this file's preface in the skill.
337: 
338: **What it checks (three-state OK / BAD / UNCERTAIN):**
339: - **Group A — on-disk artifacts:** verification_log has ≥1 `- iter` entry ·
340:   acceptance.md first line `> cap=5  stall=3×` · every cited media/screenshot
341:   exists >0 bytes · assert_artifacts.py actually runs and exits 0.
342: - **Group B — narration markers in your text:** `[Verification Gate]` ·
343:   `HARD-GATE-1: NO-TEST-NO-DONE` · `HARD-GATE-2: SCRIPT-ONLY` ·
344:   `[Covenant Recall]` · `[Memory Gate]` · `[Convergence]` · 8-column table
345:   header · `assert_artifacts.py: pass=N/fail=0` · `covenant_recall: pass` ·
346:   `memory_gate: pass`.
347: - **Group C — claim↔artifact cross-checks of the gate line (triage):**
348:   `Loop executed` ↔ iter entries · `Iterations` ↔ log count · `Media graded` ↔
349:   files on disk · `E2E depth` ↔ `tests/workflows/*.trace.log` · `TDD RED` ↔
350:   `- iter N FAIL:` · `Fresh-run` ↔ commit time vs log write · `Code review`
351:   ↔ dispatch/reason · script-only ↔ bash (raw `npm run build`/`vite`/`npm
352:   start`/`uvicorn`/`pkill -f` forbidden) · R1/R1b reads ↔ read tool calls ·
353:   verifier announcement · COV-9 entry · HARD-GATE-1/2 values.
354: 
355: **Report:** written to `tests/gate_audit.md` at session idle (refreshed at
356: every session idle, which fires after EVERY assistant turn). The FULL final
357: audit runs only when the session text contains the completion markers
358: (`[Verification Gate]` or the 8-column table header); in-progress turns get
359: the warn-only mid audit and never set BLOCKING (multi-turn tasks must not
360: deadlock). First line is the verdict:
361: ```
362: AUDIT: BAD=n UNCERTAIN=n escalate=true|false reasons=[BAD,UNCERTAIN,HIGH-RISK,SAMPLING] BLOCKING=yes|no
363: ```
364: - `BLOCKING=yes` latches RED at the project root (persisted per project root in
365:   `.vibeweaver/audit-state.json`, with the latching session's ID embedded in the
366:   latch value) and the next
367:   non-test `write`/`edit` throws GATE-BLOCKED (`tool.execute.before`).
368:   **The latch is scoped to the session that earned it:**
369:   - The latching session stays blocked while it continues — self-correct:
370:     repair each `[BAD]` item (fix the evidence, append `- audit-fix: …` /
371:     `- audit-ruling: …` entries to `tests/verification_log.md`) and re-emit
372:     a corrected `[Verification Gate]` line; the audit re-runs at every idle
373:     and on every write. No human action is needed.
374:   - Session-scoped, D3 (2026-10-15): a FOREIGN session's writes never clear
375:     the latch (the old takeover release was a bypass). Releases: the latching
376:     session's OWN next task (new-task key below), the TTL (`redTtlHours`,
377:     default 24h), or legacy (pre session-scoping) state. `tests/` stays
378:     writable throughout. Every release is recorded — `redReleases` (bounded
379:     to 5), the app log, and the report's `## Stale RED releases` — never
380:     silently dropped.
381:   - **Same-session new-task key (2026-10-02, multi-wave DOC→CODE deadlock):**
382:     the first action of a new task is writing `tests/acceptance.md` (Step 1,
383:     `tests/` is writable under the latch) — an acceptance rewrite whose
384:     floor(mtime) is strictly AFTER the latch `ts` releases on the session's
385:     next gated write/idle, journaled `new-task` (an already-expired latch
386:     journals `ttl-expiry`; the dominant fact wins). Same-ms ties resolve to
387:     "no release"; a backward clock step is the remaining skew corner
388:     (fail-safe: stays blocked). The old wave's debt stays in
389:     `tests/gate_audit.md`; the new wave's completion claim re-checks
390:     everything (re-arm leg below).
391:   - **BAD-signature guard (no re-latch treadmill; r2 hardening):** a final
392:     audit scores the WHOLE buffer, so re-audits of an unchanged failure must
393:     not re-latch. Re-latch requires a genuinely new failure: the *session
394:     signature* (sorted BAD ids, keyed PER SESSION — root keys would amnesty
395:     a different session's first failure) or the *completion-marker count*
396:     (grows by one per NEW claim — a new claim re-arms even with an identical
397:     signature; same-claim re-audits stay suppressed). A live latch is never
398:     refreshed (TTL backstop stays real); a GREEN final clears the latch,
399:     signature and count. Boundaries: two claims >150KB apart can trim the
400:     earlier marker (head 20KB kept) — the count leg misses one re-arm, the
401:     signature leg still fires; quoted marker mentions count too — fail-closed,
402:     journaled. Pre-deploy latches carry no signature and may re-latch once
403:     before the guard records theirs — self-healing in one cycle.
404:   - Any `test`/`tests` directory in the project (top-level `tests/`,
405:     `dev/tests/`, `src/test/`, …) stays writable while RED, so the
406:     evidence-fix path can never deadlock.
407: - `escalate=true` → the Tier-2 contract below applies.
408: 
409: **Tier-2 escalation contract (escalate=true — YOUR obligation, NOT optional):**
410: 1. Read `tests/gate_audit.md` IN FULL: every `[BAD]` line names the broken
411:    artifact/claim; every `[UNCERTAIN]` line names what could not be verified
412:    mechanically, with a review packet (`<packet id="C9">...`) of the evidence.
413: 2. Dispatch a **fresh-brain reviewer** (opencode `task` tool, READ-ONLY,
414:    per §A4.9 verdict contract — Strengths · Critical/Important/Minor with
415:    file:line · Assessment) with ONLY: `tests/gate_audit.md` +
416:    `tests/acceptance.md` + `tests/verification_log.md` + the review packets.
417:    Ask it to answer, per packet: *did this step genuinely happen, on the
418:    evidence in the transcript/artifacts?*
419: 3. Fix Critical/Important findings; log every fix as
420:    `- audit-fix: <finding> | changed: <file>` in `tests/verification_log.md`
421:    (machine-recognizable prefix, same format discipline as `diagnosis:`).
422:    A false positive gets `- audit-ruling: <packet> — false positive, reason: …`
423:    — never silently delete an audit line.
424: 4. Re-run the audit (any write re-checks; or read gate_audit.md after the
425:    next write) until `BLOCKING=no`. `escalate` may persist on SAMPLING —
426:    that is by design (asymmetry rule: an all-green mechanical report is NOT
427:    a clearance; ~10% of sessions are escalated by hash regardless of
428:    verdicts to catch ritual compliance — reviewer cost is the price).
429: 
430: **Scope discipline:** sessions that never loaded the vibeweaver skill are
431: not audited (subagent reviewers, unrelated chats) — silent. Doc-only tasks
432: emit the gate line with `na`/`no` values; the audit accepts those claims at
433: face value (no artifact demanded). Disable per-run: `VIBEWEAVER_AUDIT=off`.
434: 
435: **Loop-guard (degenerate-generation watchdog):** the same text observation
436: channel also watches for runaway output, independent of the artifact audit.
437: Five shapes, detected the moment they emerge from the assistant text stream
438: (reasoning parts ride the same machinery in their own buffer and episode budget):
439: (a) an identical line-group repeating at the tail — period derived from the
440: data (any block period up to 640 lines within the 96KB tail window, i.e.
441: realistic code up to ~50 chars/line), multi-line groups at ≥3×; a single
442: repeated line needs ≥4× and punctuation-only separator lines are ignored
443: (identical banner/log lines ×3 are legitimate codegen); (b) a trailing run of
444: ≥12 bare tokens stepping +1 — integers (`1,2,…,179`) or bijective base-26
445: letters (`a,b,…,kf`); (c) line-sparse (no-newline) tails — a char-level
446: suffix period: the same ≥32-char string repeated ≥4× (with a letter/digit;
447: short sub-period streams are caught at their ≥32-char super-period), e.g. a
448: sentence streamed back-to-back with no line breaks; trailing whitespace/newline
449: noise is normalized at scan entry on every detector path, and a ≥256-char last
450: line enters the scan even under newline-rich context); (d) counter-bearing
451: line runs — ≥16 consecutive tail lines with identical non-digit shape whose
452: every digit run steps strictly +1 (`The backlog item {i} …` walls; strict +1
453: excludes timestamp logs and `page N of M`; a single trailing status line does
454: not mask the run); (e) punctuation-only walls — a punct-only suffix period
455: counts only once the wall's own trailing punctuation run is ≥2KB (a big
456: report ending in a short rule/banner and ASCII-art separators stay clean);
457: plus a visible-text-only ceiling: >256KB fires `runaway` (re-armed per 256KB;
458: `loopGuardTurnCeilingBytes`, min 64KB; reasoning excluded, independent 1MB
459: backstop `loopGuardReasoningCeilingBytes` (min 256KB); id-less hosts reset at
460: the user boundary — unseen-shape backstop). Repeated JSX/HTML
461: elements ×3 and pure-punctuation runs stay clean by the same bar. On trigger
462: the plugin interrupts the session (v1 `session.abort` / v2
463: `session.interrupt({continue:false})`) and posts a corrective prompt naming
464: the pattern (restate the task in one line + the single next concrete step).
465: One intervention per degeneration episode (re-arms after clean text or a NEW
466: assistant turn — fresh-turn re-degeneration gets its own intervention;
467: same-turn continuation never re-fires), budget 2 per session per
468: channel (further episodes are log-only, config
469: `loopGuardMaxInterventions` in `audit.json`). Near-misses excluded:
470: numbered lists with content (`1. step`) are not bare tokens;
471: a 2× repetition is below the bar. Disable per-run:
472: `VIBEWEAVER_LOOPGUARD=off`.
473: 
474: **C8 self-clearing rule:** a forbidden raw command (C8) flags only ONCE per
475: project root (command-hash dedup, persisted in `.vibeweaver/audit-state.json`
476: `c8Flagged`). Immutable session history can never pin a session in a
477: permanent RED latch — the latch clears on the next GREEN audit; every NEW
478: distinct forbidden command still flags. The dedup is persisted only by the
479: FINAL audit: a mid-phase warning never consumes the one-shot, so a forbidden
480: command run mid-task still latches when the completion audit lands.
481: 
482: **Config lives OUTSIDE the agent's write scope:** global only —
483: `~/.config/opencode/vibeweaver/audit.json` (overrides DEFAULTS:
484: `samplingRate` · `escOnUncertain` · `escOnHighRisk` · `forbiddenRaw`).
485: A project-local `.vibeweaver/audit.json` is DELIBERATELY IGNORED — the agent
486: can write it, and a model under prompt injection would use it to disable its
487: own auditor (the optimizer must never have write access to its own objective
488: function).
489: 
490: **Known boundaries (by design, not bugs):** the audit proves tokens, files
491: and orderings — never intent. `na`/`no` claims are accepted at face value;
492: A4.9 trigger classification rests on the model's self-assessment; process
493: compliance is not outcome correctness. Those are the reviewer's (and the
494: user's) judgments — the audit's job is to make the machine-checkable layer
495: honest. A truncated/aborted session's buffered text may be incomplete
496: (head/tail caps), so its final audit can latch RED on partial evidence —
497: that is the latch being conservative, and it is bounded precisely because
498: of this: it yields to the session's own next task (new-task key) or expires
499: with its TTL (D3: a FOREIGN session's writes never clear it); is fully
500: recorded; its re-audit cannot feed on an unchanged failure signature; and
501: the evidence path (tests/) stays writable so it can never dead-lock a fix.

1: # MEMORY_RULES.md — Project Memory Subsystem Rules
2: 
3: Companion file for the `vibeweaver` skill. This file is referenced by `SKILL.md`
4: §A7 and holds the **detailed operational rules** for the `memory/MEMORY.md`
5: index, topic files, trust tiers, state flow, pre-change guardrails,

13: 
14: ## A7.1 MEMORY.md — The Index
15: 
16: `memory/MEMORY.md` is the **entrypoint**. It is loaded into context at the
17: start of every session. It acts as a table of contents — not the memory content
18: itself.
19: 
20: **Format:**
21: ```markdown
22: # Project Memory Index
23: 
24: ## User Context
25: - [User Role & Preferences](user_role_prefs.md) — Senior backend engineer, prefers explicit error handling
26: - [Code Style Preferences](user_code_style.md) — Always use TypeScript strict mode, no any
27: 
28: ## Feedback — Validated Approaches
29: - [Keep Using Test DB](feedback_testing.md) — Use test containers, never mock DB in integration tests
30: - [Bundled PRs for Auth](feedback_auth_prs.md) — Single PR for tightly coupled auth refactors
31: 
32: ## Feedback — Corrections
33: - [Don't Use Raw SQL in Routes](feedback_no_raw_sql.md) — Always go through repository layer
34: 
35: ## Project Context
36: - [Q4 Deadlines](project_q4_deadlines.md) — Merge freeze 2026-03-05, release cutoff 2026-03-12
37: 
38: ## External References
39: - [Grafana Dashboard](reference_grafana.md) — Production metrics at grafana.example.com/d/abc123
40: 
41: ## Fix Tracking
42: - ⛔ [Forbidden: Direct DB Access from Routes](fix_forbidden_db_routes.md) — Never query DB from route handlers
43: - ✅ [Fix: Login Timeout](fix_login_timeout.md) — Session TTL mismatch between auth service and gateway
44: - ⏳ [Fix: Search Pagination](fix_search_pagination.md) — Pending user confirmation
45: 
46: ## Key Dependencies & Conventions
47: - `auth/` module must be loaded before `routes/` (circular dependency resolved via lazy import)
48: - WebSocket connections require explicit heartbeat every 30s
49: ```
50: 
51: **Caps:**
52: - **Loading cap:** **200 lines** or **25,000 bytes** (25KB) — whichever comes first. If the index is larger, **truncate on load** and append a warning:
53:   ```
54:   > WARNING: MEMORY.md is over the limit. Only part was loaded. Consolidate entries or move detail into topic files.
55:   ```
56: - **Consolidation trigger:** When the index grows beyond **150 lines** or **20KB**, run consolidation at the end of the session (see A7.13).
57: - Keep each index line to one line under ~150 characters
58:

61: ## A7.2 Topic Files — One Per Memory Entry
62: 
63: Each memory entry is a **separate `.md` file** with YAML frontmatter. This enables on-demand loading — only the most relevant topic files are loaded per session.
64: 
65: **Frontmatter format:**
66: ```yaml
67: ---
68: name: Short descriptive title
69: description: One-line description used to decide relevance in future sessions — be specific
70: type: user | feedback | project | reference | fix
71: date: 2026-06-28
72: status: ⛔ | ✅ | ⏳   # Required for fix type only
73: commit: abc1234      # Required for fix type only — short hash of the change this memory describes
74: file_refs:          # Optional — for fix entries that cite specific files; enables stale-ref auto-detection (A7.6 rule 8)
75:   - path: backend/app/auth/config.py
76:     range: "40-50"         # approx line range cited
77:     sha_at_time: 8f3a2c1   # git blob sha at fix time: git rev-parse <commit>:<path>
78: last_validated: 2026-06-28 # Optional — last session that re-verified this entry
79: ---
80: ```
81: 
82: **Body structure (feedback/project types):**
83: - Lead with the **rule or fact** itself
84: - **Why:** — the reason (past incident, constraint, strong preference)
85: - **How to apply:** — when/where this guidance kicks in, edge cases
86: 
87: **Example — feedback type:**
88: ```markdown
89: ---
90: name: Don't Mock DB in Integration Tests
91: description: Never use in-memory SQLite or mocked repositories in tests that touch the database
92: type: feedback
93: date: 2026-06-28
94: ---
95: 
96: # Don't Mock the Database in Integration Tests
97: 
98: **Why:** Prior incident where mock/prod divergence masked a broken migration. The mock SQLite accepted NULL in a NOT NULL column that PostgreSQL rejected.
99: 
100: **How to apply:** When writing tests for DB-touching code, use test containers or a real test database. Mocking is acceptable only for pure unit tests that don't exercise SQL.
101: ```
102: 
103: **Example — project type:**
104: ```markdown
105: ---
106: name: Q4 Merge Freeze
107: description: Team release schedule with merge freeze and cutoff dates for Q4 2026
108: type: project
109: date: 2026-03-01
110: ---
111: 
112: # Q4 Merge Freeze
113: 
114: Merge freeze begins **2026-03-05**. Mobile team is cutting a release branch.
115: 
116: **How to apply:** Flag any non-critical PR work scheduled after that date. Critical bugfixes still allowed with release-manager approval.
117: ```
118: 
119: **Example — fix type (unverified):**
120: ```markdown
121: ---
122: name: Fix Login Timeout
123: description: Session TTL mismatch causing premature logout on the login page
124: type: fix
125: date: 2026-06-28
126: status: ⏳
127: commit: a1b2c3d
128: ---
129: 
130: # Fix Login Timeout
131: 
132: **Problem:** Users reported being logged out after ~5 minutes of inactivity on the login page.
133: 
134: **Root Cause:** Session TTL was set to 300s in auth service but 3600s in API gateway. The gateway's longer TTL masked the issue until the auth service expired the session first.
135: 
136: **Correct Fix:** Aligned both TTLs to 1800s in `backend/app/auth/config.py:42` and `gateway/nginx.conf:15`.
137: 
138: **Failed Approaches (DO NOT retry):**
139: - Increasing only the auth service TTL without checking gateway — still caused mismatch
140: - Adding a client-side refresh timer — papered over the issue, didn't fix root cause
141: 
142: **Files:** `backend/app/auth/config.py`, `gateway/nginx.conf`
143: **Status:** ⏳ Pending — awaiting user confirmation
144: ```

150: ## A7.3 Memory Types
151: 
152: Memories are constrained to types capturing context NOT derivable from the current project state:
153: 
154: | Type | What to Save | When to Save |
155: |------|-------------|--------------|
156: | **user** | User's role, goals, skill level, preferences | When you learn any detail about the user's perspective or expertise |
157: | **feedback** | Corrections AND confirmations on approach | When user says "don't do X", OR confirms "yes exactly, keep doing that" |
158: | **project** | Ongoing work, goals, deadlines, team context | When you learn who is doing what, why, or by when. Convert relative dates to absolute |
159: | **reference** | Pointers to external resources (issue tracker, dashboards, docs) | When you learn where to find up-to-date information outside the project |
160: | **fix** | Bug fixes and modifications — root cause, correct fix, failed attempts | After every code change (see State Flow Rules below) |
161: 
162: **Critical: Record from both failure AND success.** If you only save corrections, you will drift away from approaches the user has already validated.
163:

165: 
166: ## A7.4 What NOT to Save
167: 
168: - Code patterns, conventions, architecture, file paths, or project structure — derivable by reading the project
169: - Git history, recent changes, or who-changed-what — `git log` / `git blame` are authoritative
170: - Debugging solutions or fix recipes — the fix is in the code; the commit message has the context
171: - Anything already documented in README or other project docs
172: - Ephemeral task details: in-progress work, temporary state, current conversation context
173:

176: ## A7.5 Trust Tiers (for fix entries)
177: 
178: | Tier | Trust Level | Purpose |
179: |------|-------------|---------|
180: | ⛔ **Forbidden** | Highest — hard constraints | Methods proven to fail. Agent MUST NOT retry. |
181: | ✅ **Verified** | High — confirmed by user | Root cause, correct fix, failed approaches. Primary reference. |
182: | ⏳ **Unverified** | Low — may be wrong | Agent's modifications awaiting user validation. Informational only. |
183: | ❌ **Failed**    | Negation of ⏳       | An ⏳ that failed a later check or got reimplemented badly. Same hard constraints as permissibility. |
184: 
185: **Core principle: unverified modifications are NOT facts. Never treat ⏳ entries as proven solutions.**

189: ## A7.6 On Every Skill Invocation — Memory Loading
190: 
191: When the skill triggers, load project memory in this order:
192: 
193: 1. **Check if `memory/MEMORY.md` exists**
194:    - YES → Read it (first 200 lines / 25KB automatically loaded via truncation)
195:    - NO → Check if old `MODIFY.html` exists. If yes, **migrate it** to the `memory/` directory structure (see A7.11). If neither exists, this is a fresh project — create `memory/MEMORY.md` with template from [MEMORY_TEMPLATES.md](MEMORY_TEMPLATES.md).
196: 
197: 2. **Scan the index** — For each section (User Context, Feedback, Project Context, External References, Fix Tracking), note the entries relevant to the current task.
198: 
199: 3. **Search before selecting** — Extract keywords from the user's request (problem symptom, feature name, file/module names, error messages). Use the `grep` tool to search `memory/*.md` for topic files whose names, descriptions, or bodies mention those keywords. This catches relevant memories whose index descriptions may not be obvious.
200: 
201: 4. **Select top 3-5 most relevant topic files** — Combine index scan + search results. Prioritize in this order:
202:    - ⛔ **Forbidden** entries touching the same area
203:    - ❌ **Failed** attempts with the same symptom
204:    - ✅ **Verified** fixes for the same files or problem
205:    - ⏳ **Unverified** attempts for the same problem
206:    - **Feedback** entries about the relevant approach or file
207:    Load only those files.
208: 
209: 5. **Verify references before trusting** — For any loaded memory that names specific files, functions, classes, configs, or line numbers, read the current code to confirm they still exist and mean the same thing. If a reference is stale, update or remove the memory entry and note the staleness.
210: 
211: 6. **Check for staleness** — For any loaded topic file with a `date` older than 14 days from today, display:
212:    ```
213:    > ⚠️ This memory is N days old. Memories are point-in-time observations — claims about code behavior or file:line citations may be outdated. Verify against current code before acting.
214:    ```
215: 
216: 7. **Check ⏳ Unverified entries** — If the user's current request overlaps an ⏳ fix entry in problem, symptom, affected file, or attempted solution, treat it as a failure signal. Mark that entry ❌ before attempting a new direction (see A7.7 Implicit Failure Detection).
217: 
218: 8. **✅ Verified staleness rule** — a ✅ entry is NOT immune to staleness; it only means it was verified at the commit recorded. When loading a ✅ fix entry:
219:    - If its `last_validated` is absent or >14 days old → mark it ⏳ again with a `stale: needs re-verification` note and re-verify before trusting.
220:    - If it has `file_refs[*].sha_at_time` and that ≠ current `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` (or the ref is absent and the file moved) → same treatment: demote to ⏳ with a stale-refs note; re-verify code references against current code before acting on it.
221:    - A stale ✅ provides context but MUST NOT be relied on for downstream decisions until re-verified this session.
222:

225: ## A7.7 State Flow Rules (for fix-tracking entries)
226: 
227: ```
228: Agent modifies code
229:   ↓
230: Agent runs Playwright / automated tests
231:   ├─ Tests FAIL → create fix topic file with status ❌, try different direction
232:   └─ Tests PASS → create fix topic file with status ⏳ (NOT as ✅)
233:         ↓
234:   Next session begins:
235:     ├─ User gives same/similar prompt → auto-mark ⏳ as ❌, try different direction
236:     ├─ User explicitly says "still broken" → mark ⏳ as ❌, try different direction
237:     └─ User confirms "works" / no further complaint → promote to ✅ Verified
238: ```
239: 
240: **Implicit Failure Detection: if the user's current request overlaps an ⏳ fix entry in problem, symptom, affected file, or attempted solution, treat it as a failure signal. Mark that entry ❌ before attempting a new direction.**
241: 
242: **≥3 failures on same problem → escalate all failed methods to a ⛔ Forbidden topic file.**

246: ## A7.8 Pre-Change Guardrails
247: 
248: Before implementing any change:
249: 1. Check ⛔ **Forbidden** entries — do NOT use any listed method
250: 2. Scan ✅ **Verified** fix entries for files you are about to touch — learn from confirmed solutions
251: 3. Scan ⏳ **Unverified** fix entries for the current problem — if a pending entry exists, acknowledge it and explain why this attempt takes a different direction
252: 4. Check **Feedback** entries for relevant guidance on approach
253: 5. When touching a ⛔ flagged area, explicitly state why your approach avoids the forbidden pattern

257: ## A7.9 Post-Session Memory Writing ★ NON-NEGOTIABLE
258: 
259: **At the end of every session, before outputting the completion table, you MUST review and write memories:**
260: 
261: 1. **Review the conversation** — Identify new information worth persisting across sessions
262: 2. **Write topic files** for each new entry in `memory/` with proper frontmatter
263: 3. **Update MEMORY.md index** — Add pointer lines for new entries. Remove pointers to stale/removed entries
264: 4. **Fix-tracking rules:**
265:    - Write fix entries as `status: ⏳` if tests passed, `status: ❌` if tests failed
266:    - **Never write `status: ✅`** — only user confirmation can verify a fix
267:    - Include the commit short hash in the frontmatter (`commit: abc1234`) for every fix entry
268:    - Include **Failed Approaches** and **Rejected Alternatives** in fix topic bodies so future sessions do not rediscover the same dead ends
269:    - If ≥3 failures preceded this fix, create/update a ⛔ Forbidden entry
270: 5. **Record feedback memories** when user corrects or confirms approach during the session
271: 6. **Record project memories** when you learn about goals, deadlines, or team context
272: 7. **Check MEMORY.md caps** — If index exceeds 150 lines or 20KB, consolidate before adding more
273: 8. **Resolve the task working note** — distill `tests/working_note.md` (§A7.15) into the permanent topic files, then delete it (machine-checked by group 19 on the `--final` run)
274: 
275: **The checklist item "Memory topic file written to memory/" is MANDATORY for
276: any task that produced a lesson — lesson-triggered, not per-task ritual.**
277: Lesson-less tasks (Class DOC / trivial changes, §V11.3) state
278: `- memory: na (<why no lesson>)` in `tests/verification_log.md` instead of
279: writing filler topics (A7.1 "what NOT to save" — a forced empty topic is
280: worse than none).

284: ## A7.10 Final Memory Gate ★ NON-NEGOTIABLE
285: 
286: Before outputting the completion table, you MUST pass this gate. If any check fails, return to A7.9 and fix it before declaring the task complete.
287: 
288: 1. **Memory files exist** — At least one new or updated topic file exists in `memory/` for this session (unless the task was purely informational and produced nothing persistable).
289: 2. **Index updated** — `memory/MEMORY.md` contains a pointer to the new topic file(s), and the index is under 200 lines / 25KB.
290: 3. **Fix entries have commit** — Every `type: fix` topic file written this session includes `commit: <short-hash>` in its frontmatter. **History-rewrite waves (Class-E `git filter-repo`, ENGINEERING_STD §A10.1) must complete the commit-map hash remap BEFORE passing this gate** — every `commit:` cited in `memory/**` and `tests/verification_log.md` is rewritten from `.git/filter-repo/commit-map` (copy, never retype a hash), then this gate re-checks them.
291: 4. **No stale references introduced** — Any file/function/line cited in new memories was verified against current code during this session.
292: 5. **Scratchpad cleaned (legacy)** — the pre-§A7.15 `memory/.session-scratchpad.md` is superseded by tests/working_note.md; if a legacy scratchpad exists, delete it after permanent memories are written.
293: 6. **Working note resolved** — If `tests/working_note.md` was created (§A7.15), its persistable content was distilled into the topic files written this session and the file itself is deleted. The completion-time `assert_artifacts.py --final` run (group 19) machine-checks the deletion.
294: 
295: **Failure response:**
296: - If a memory should have been written but was not, write it now and re-run this gate.
297: - If you genuinely have nothing persistable (rare), explicitly state "No memory written — task was informational only" in the completion table's `What Changed` column.
298: 
299: **Explicit reporting:** In the line immediately before the completion table, output a single summary line:
300: ```
301: [Memory Gate] Passed: N new/updated topic file(s) | Index updated: yes/no | Commit hashes present: yes/no/N/A | Scratchpad cleaned: yes/no/N/A
302: ```
303: or, when nothing persistable was produced (§V11.3 lesson-triggered):
304: ```
305: [Memory Gate] na (<why no lesson>) — gate line field: memory_gate: na
306: ```
307: Do not output the completion table until this line is present and all answers are truthful.

311: ## A7.11 Promoting to Verified & Migration from Old Format
312: 
313: **Promoting a fix to ✅ Verified:**
314: When user confirms a fix works (or next session has no complaint about it):
315: 1. Change `status: ⏳` → `status: ✅` in the topic file's frontmatter
316: 2. Fill in **Root Cause**, **Failed Approaches**, and **Rejected Alternatives** in the body
317: 3. Add the verified commit short hash to the frontmatter (`commit: abc1234`)
318: 4. Add `file_refs` (path + range + `sha_at_time` from `git rev-parse <commit>:<path>`) for every file cited, and set `last_validated: <today>` — this makes the ✅ entry self-aging (A7.6 rule 8)
319: 5. Update the index line to show ✅ instead of ⏳
320: 6. If ≥3 failures preceded the fix, also create a ⛔ Forbidden entry
321: 
322: **Migrating from old MODIFY.html / MODIFY_COMPACT.html:**
323: If an old project has `MODIFY.html` or `MODIFY_COMPACT.html` but no `memory/` directory:
324: 1. Read the old file(s) completely
325: 2. Split each logical entry into a separate `memory/*.md` topic file with proper frontmatter
326: 3. Create `memory/MEMORY.md` with pointer lines for all entries
327: 4. Do NOT delete the old HTML files — they serve as archive
328: 5. This is a one-time migration; subsequent sessions use `memory/`

332: ## A7.12 Multi-Level Memory (User-Global + Project-Local)
333: 
334: **Two scopes are loaded and merged on session start:**
335: 
336: | Scope | Path | Content | Priority |
337: |-------|------|---------|----------|
338: | **User-global** | `~/.config/opencode/vibeweaver/memory/` | Cross-project user preferences, coding style, general feedback | Lower |
339: | **Project-local** | `<project>/memory/` | Project-specific architecture, fix tracking, team context | Higher |
340: 
341: **Loading order:** User-global MEMORY.md first → Project-local MEMORY.md second. If the same topic exists in both, project-local wins.
342: 
343: **What goes in user-global memory:**
344: - User's preferred languages, frameworks, and tools
345: - General coding conventions (e.g., "always use TypeScript strict mode")
346: - Feedback that applies across all projects (e.g., "never use `any` type")
347: - The user's role and expertise level
348: 
349: **What goes in project-local memory:**
350: - Everything else — fix tracking, project deadlines, project-specific conventions, external references
351: 
352: **On session start:** Read user-global MEMORY.md first, then project-local MEMORY.md. Select top 3-5 most relevant topic files combined across both scopes.

356: ## A7.13 Consolidation Rules
357: 
358: When `memory/` has **>15 topic files** or **MEMORY.md exceeds 150 lines or 20KB**:
359: 
360: 1. **Keep all** ⛔ Forbidden entries verbatim — these are hard constraints
361: 2. **Keep all** ✅ Verified fix entries
362: 3. **Keep all** User Context and Feedback entries — these are high-value
363: 4. **Prune ⏳ entries** — Keep only ⏳ entries from the last 14 days. Delete older unverified entries (the code they reference has likely changed)
364: 5. **Merge related entries** — e.g., two feedback entries about testing can become one consolidated topic file
365: 6. **Remove stale references** — If a file or function mentioned in a memory no longer exists, delete or update the entry
366: 7. **Update MEMORY.md** — Remove pointers to deleted entries, add pointers to merged entries
367: 8. **Write a `memory/.consolidation-log.md`** — Record: date, what was merged/removed, old entry filenames
368: 9. **Cross-project ⛔ promotion** — If the same ⛔ Forbidden pattern exists in ≥2 projects' memories, propose to the user promoting it into the skill-level rules (ENGINEERING_STD.md / the skill's rule files). Project memory stays the record; a lesson recurring everywhere belongs one level up. Never edit skill rules silently — the user approves skill-level changes
369: 
370: **Do NOT consolidate mid-session.** Only at session end, after memories are written.
371:

374: ## A7.14 Retrospective Memory & Backtracking
375: 
376: The memory system is only effective if previous attempts are actively recalled before new attempts are made. Follow these rules to maximize retrospective value:
377: 
378: 1. **Activate memory before fixing** — Before implementing any fix or new approach for a problem, explicitly list all prior attempts found in memory (⛔ Forbidden, ❌ Failed, ✅ Verified, ⏳ Unverified) that relate to the same symptom, file, or feature. State why each is not suitable for the current attempt.
379: 
380: 2. **Record every direction, not just failures** — When a fix passes tests, the topic file must still include a **Failed Approaches** or **Rejected Alternatives** section listing directions that were considered and rejected, even if they were not fully implemented. This prevents future sessions from independently rediscovering the same dead ends.
381: 
382: 3. **Mid-session backtracking scratchpad** — superseded by the task working note (§A7.15): use `tests/working_note.md` instead of `memory/.session-scratchpad.md`; its hypothesis ledger carries the same four fields (current hypothesis / tried+result / next direction / memories consulted) in a machine-gated form.
383: 
384: 4. **Link fixes to commits** — Every fix topic file must include the commit hash of the change in its frontmatter (`commit: abc1234`). This allows future retrospective checks to compare the memory against the exact code state.
385: 
386: 5. **Escalate early on repeated dead ends** — If you find yourself considering an approach that was already recorded as ❌ Failed or ⛔ Forbidden, stop. Do not retry it without a genuinely new insight. Document the new insight before proceeding.
387: 
388: 6. **Promote ⏳ to ❌ on divergence, not just failure** — If a later task contradicts or supersedes an ⏳ fix (e.g., the user changes requirements, or the architecture shifts), mark the old ⏳ entry as ❌ and explain why it no longer applies.

391: ## A7.15 Task Working Memory — tests/working_note.md ★
392: 
393: The layer between the evidence chronicle and curated memory. `tests/` log
394: files answer "what happened" (append-only); `memory/` answers "what is true
395: about this project" (curated, session-end). The working note answers **"what
396: holds RIGHT NOW in this task"** — the cognitive-state ledger that a context
397: reset (compaction / new session / §3.3 re-entry) would otherwise have to
398: expensively reconstruct from the log tail.
399: 
400: **When to create:** Lane M/L tasks, and any task that reaches a second
401: iteration or a first FAIL. Lane S single-pass tasks may skip (state the
402: skip). Class DOC lesson-less tasks may skip.
403: 
404: **Form (≤50 lines, REWRITTEN each update — it is state, not chronicle; git
405: history is the audit trail):**
406: 
407: ```
408: # Working Note — <task> (updated: iter N / <time>)
409: ## Hypothesis ledger
410: confirmed: <what evidence proved true>
411: doubted:   <leaning but unproven>
412: excluded:  <falsified directions — one falsifiable clause each>
413: open:      <unresolved questions>
414: consulted: <memory topics read this task>
415: ## Key locations
416: <file:line — one clause why it matters>   (max ~8)
417: ## Dead ends this task
418: ❌ <direction — one clause why it died>
419: ## Next action
420: <one line>
421: ```
422: 
423: **Lifecycle (binding):**
424: 1. Create after §A4.1 Step 1 (acceptance criteria) when the create-rule
425:    above fires.
426: 2. Update at every FAIL diagnosis, every iteration boundary, and BEFORE any
427:    anticipated compaction — the note is what survives it.
428: 3. Log lifecycle events as `- working-note:` lines in the current task block
429:    (group 20 machine-checks the create rule: ≥2 iterations or a FAIL owes
430:    them, or a stated `- working-note: na (<why>)`). §3.3 re-entry reads it
431:    FIRST among tests/ artifacts (after
432:    `paused_state.md` if present, before `acceptance.md` + log tail).
433: 4. Task end: distill persistable content into `memory/` topic files per
434:    A7.9 (the note is A7.9's primary input), then DELETE the file. The
435:    completion-time `python3 tests/assert_artifacts.py --final` run
436:    machine-checks the deletion (group 19); mid-task runs (no `--final`,
437:    incl. the physical gate) tolerate it. The A7.10 Memory Gate reports the
438:    resolution (check 6).
439: 
440: **Deterministic delivery (wave21, harness-side, best-effort):** the
441: vibeweaver-gate plugin delivers the note for you — its content is pushed into
442: the compaction prompt at every pre-summary (`experimental.session.compacting`),
443: re-injected on that session's next model request after every
444: `session.compacted` event (system transform, session-keyed — verified live on
445: opencode 1.18.35), and pointed to by a one-line cue on the session's first
446: gated write. Delivery counts land in `.vibeweaver/state.json`
447: (`memoryDeliveries`); a harness-owned snapshot (`.vibeweaver/memory-snapshot.json`)
448: keeps boundary delivery working even if the note file itself disappears mid-task. These channels are host features and degrade quietly
449: where absent — treat them as reliable when present, never as a license to
450: skip the note discipline. Consequence for the author: **keep the note FRESH**
451: — the harness delivers whatever is in the file verbatim; a stale ledger is
452: delivered stale. Update it at iteration/FAIL boundaries rather than relying
453: on "remember before compaction".
454: 
455: **Relationship to C8 (outer loop):** the working note is ITEM-scoped state
456: (dies when the backlog item completes); `tests/progress.txt` is the
457: cross-item chronicle (append-only); `memory/` is cross-task curated. Three
458: time scales, no overlap.

460: ## A7.16 Cue-Anchored Triggers — memory frontmatter `triggers:` ★
461: 
462: Task-start grep (§3.2) cannot cover the moments that matter MID-task —
463: "about to edit a file with a known trap" is exactly when the lesson is
464: needed, and voluntary mid-task retrieval is empirically near zero. So the
465: trigger is anchored to the PATH and delivered by the gate plugin at the
466: edit moment (mechanism, not memory of the rule).
467: 
468: **Declaring triggers** — optional frontmatter field on any topic file,
469: both forms accepted:
470: 
471: ```
472: ---
473: type: fix
474: status: ❌
475: triggers:
476:   - "src/auth/**"
477: ---
478: ```
479: or inline: `triggers: ["db/**", "src/repos/**"]`
480: 
481: Glob semantics: `**/` crosses directories, `*` within a path segment,
482: `?` one character; matched against the project-relative path.
483: 
484: **Delivery (vibeweaver-gate plugin):** after a successful write/edit, the
485: plugin scans `memory/*.md` frontmatter; each matching topic injects ONE
486: line into the tool result —
487: `[GATE-WARNING (vibeweaver-cue)] memory cue: memory/<file> (<trust>) matches this path — read it before editing: <heading>`
488: — budgeted at 3 notes, pointer-only (progressive disclosure: READ the
489: topic before continuing; the cue is delivery, the topic is the content).
490: Editing a path under `memory/` itself never cues (no self-reference).
491: Delivery is hoisted above the gate: a RED gate or an evidence-path write
492: (tests/) still carries the cue — the first write of a task is the prime
493: cue moment.
494: 
495: **Known boundaries (named, accepted):** (1) the cue is ADVISORY — injection
496: is deterministic, but whether the model then reads the topic is not
497: machine-enforced (a "must Read first" hard gate cannot cheaply verify
498: having read); (2) mutations performed through bash bypass delivery (same
499: boundary as §A4.4.2); (3) duplicate `triggers:` keys in one frontmatter
500: block are first-wins; (4) a glob's literal leading path is linted by
501: `assert_artifacts.py` group 4b — if that prefix no longer exists in the
502: repo the trigger is stale (silent non-delivery) and the assert FAILs;
503: globs starting with `**` carry no literal prefix and are exempt;
504: (5) delivery-safety caps: a glob with >2 `**` groups, >200 chars, or
505: control characters is ignored entirely (memory text compiles to regex —
506: complexity caps are the injection boundary); (6) end-to-end verified on
507: macOS/Linux only — win32 path handling is unit-pinned (CRLF fixture), not
508: machine-executed.
509: 
510: **Authoring rules:** triggers are for path-anchored operational facts
511: (gotchas, traps, fragile files) — NOT for generic project knowledge (that
512: stays grep-loaded per §3.2). Keep globs narrow (a cue that fires on every
513: edit is noise and trains cue-blindness). When the anchored code moves,
514: update the glob in the same commit (a stale trigger is a silent
515: non-delivery, same failure class as a stale reference — A7.6 rule 8
516: applies). Trust-tier semantics carry over: ⛔/❌ topics are the prime

14: ## A7.1 MEMORY.md — The Index
15: 
16: `memory/MEMORY.md` is the **entrypoint**. It is loaded into context at the
17: start of every session. It acts as a table of contents — not the memory content
18: itself.
19: 
20: **Format:**
21: ```markdown
22: # Project Memory Index
23: 
24: ## User Context
25: - [User Role & Preferences](user_role_prefs.md) — Senior backend engineer, prefers explicit error handling
26: - [Code Style Preferences](user_code_style.md) — Always use TypeScript strict mode, no any
27: 
28: ## Feedback — Validated Approaches
29: - [Keep Using Test DB](feedback_testing.md) — Use test containers, never mock DB in integration tests
30: - [Bundled PRs for Auth](feedback_auth_prs.md) — Single PR for tightly coupled auth refactors
31: 
32: ## Feedback — Corrections
33: - [Don't Use Raw SQL in Routes](feedback_no_raw_sql.md) — Always go through repository layer
34: 
35: ## Project Context
36: - [Q4 Deadlines](project_q4_deadlines.md) — Merge freeze 2026-03-05, release cutoff 2026-03-12
37: 
38: ## External References
39: - [Grafana Dashboard](reference_grafana.md) — Production metrics at grafana.example.com/d/abc123
40: 
41: ## Fix Tracking
42: - ⛔ [Forbidden: Direct DB Access from Routes](fix_forbidden_db_routes.md) — Never query DB from route handlers
43: - ✅ [Fix: Login Timeout](fix_login_timeout.md) — Session TTL mismatch between auth service and gateway
44: - ⏳ [Fix: Search Pagination](fix_search_pagination.md) — Pending user confirmation
45: 
46: ## Key Dependencies & Conventions
47: - `auth/` module must be loaded before `routes/` (circular dependency resolved via lazy import)
48: - WebSocket connections require explicit heartbeat every 30s
49: ```
50: 
51: **Caps:**
52: - **Loading cap:** **200 lines** or **25,000 bytes** (25KB) — whichever comes first. If the index is larger, **truncate on load** and append a warning:
53:   ```
54:   > WARNING: MEMORY.md is over the limit. Only part was loaded. Consolidate entries or move detail into topic files.
55:   ```
56: - **Consolidation trigger:** When the index grows beyond **150 lines** or **20KB**, run consolidation at the end of the session (see A7.13).
57: - Keep each index line to one line under ~150 characters

61: ## A7.2 Topic Files — One Per Memory Entry
62: 
63: Each memory entry is a **separate `.md` file** with YAML frontmatter. This enables on-demand loading — only the most relevant topic files are loaded per session.
64: 
65: **Frontmatter format:**
66: ```yaml
67: ---
68: name: Short descriptive title
69: description: One-line description used to decide relevance in future sessions — be specific
70: type: user | feedback | project | reference | fix
71: date: 2026-06-28
72: status: ⛔ | ✅ | ⏳   # Required for fix type only
73: commit: abc1234      # Required for fix type only — short hash of the change this memory describes
74: file_refs:          # Optional — for fix entries that cite specific files; enables stale-ref auto-detection (A7.6 rule 8)
75:   - path: backend/app/auth/config.py
76:     range: "40-50"         # approx line range cited
77:     sha_at_time: 8f3a2c1   # git blob sha at fix time: git rev-parse <commit>:<path>
78: last_validated: 2026-06-28 # Optional — last session that re-verified this entry
79: ---
80: ```
81: 
82: **Body structure (feedback/project types):**
83: - Lead with the **rule or fact** itself
84: - **Why:** — the reason (past incident, constraint, strong preference)
85: - **How to apply:** — when/where this guidance kicks in, edge cases
86: 
87: **Example — feedback type:**
88: ```markdown
89: ---
90: name: Don't Mock DB in Integration Tests
91: description: Never use in-memory SQLite or mocked repositories in tests that touch the database
92: type: feedback
93: date: 2026-06-28
94: ---
95: 
96: # Don't Mock the Database in Integration Tests
97: 
98: **Why:** Prior incident where mock/prod divergence masked a broken migration. The mock SQLite accepted NULL in a NOT NULL column that PostgreSQL rejected.
99: 
100: **How to apply:** When writing tests for DB-touching code, use test containers or a real test database. Mocking is acceptable only for pure unit tests that don't exercise SQL.
101: ```
102: 
103: **Example — project type:**
104: ```markdown
105: ---
106: name: Q4 Merge Freeze
107: description: Team release schedule with merge freeze and cutoff dates for Q4 2026
108: type: project
109: date: 2026-03-01
110: ---
111: 
112: # Q4 Merge Freeze
113: 
114: Merge freeze begins **2026-03-05**. Mobile team is cutting a release branch.
115: 
116: **How to apply:** Flag any non-critical PR work scheduled after that date. Critical bugfixes still allowed with release-manager approval.
117: ```
118: 
119: **Example — fix type (unverified):**
120: ```markdown
121: ---
122: name: Fix Login Timeout
123: description: Session TTL mismatch causing premature logout on the login page
124: type: fix
125: date: 2026-06-28
126: status: ⏳
127: commit: a1b2c3d
128: ---
129: 
130: # Fix Login Timeout
131: 
132: **Problem:** Users reported being logged out after ~5 minutes of inactivity on the login page.
133: 
134: **Root Cause:** Session TTL was set to 300s in auth service but 3600s in API gateway. The gateway's longer TTL masked the issue until the auth service expired the session first.
135: 
136: **Correct Fix:** Aligned both TTLs to 1800s in `backend/app/auth/config.py:42` and `gateway/nginx.conf:15`.
137: 
138: **Failed Approaches (DO NOT retry):**
139: - Increasing only the auth service TTL without checking gateway — still caused mismatch
140: - Adding a client-side refresh timer — papered over the issue, didn't fix root cause
141: 
142: **Files:** `backend/app/auth/config.py`, `gateway/nginx.conf`
143: **Status:** ⏳ Pending — awaiting user confirmation
144: ```

150: ## A7.3 Memory Types
151: 
152: Memories are constrained to types capturing context NOT derivable from the current project state:
153: 
154: | Type | What to Save | When to Save |
155: |------|-------------|--------------|
156: | **user** | User's role, goals, skill level, preferences | When you learn any detail about the user's perspective or expertise |
157: | **feedback** | Corrections AND confirmations on approach | When user says "don't do X", OR confirms "yes exactly, keep doing that" |
158: | **project** | Ongoing work, goals, deadlines, team context | When you learn who is doing what, why, or by when. Convert relative dates to absolute |
159: | **reference** | Pointers to external resources (issue tracker, dashboards, docs) | When you learn where to find up-to-date information outside the project |
160: | **fix** | Bug fixes and modifications — root cause, correct fix, failed attempts | After every code change (see State Flow Rules below) |
161: 
162: **Critical: Record from both failure AND success.** If you only save corrections, you will drift away from approaches the user has already validated.
163:

165: 
166: ## A7.4 What NOT to Save
167: 
168: - Code patterns, conventions, architecture, file paths, or project structure — derivable by reading the project
169: - Git history, recent changes, or who-changed-what — `git log` / `git blame` are authoritative
170: - Debugging solutions or fix recipes — the fix is in the code; the commit message has the context
171: - Anything already documented in README or other project docs
172: - Ephemeral task details: in-progress work, temporary state, current conversation context
173:

176: ## A7.5 Trust Tiers (for fix entries)
177: 
178: | Tier | Trust Level | Purpose |
179: |------|-------------|---------|
180: | ⛔ **Forbidden** | Highest — hard constraints | Methods proven to fail. Agent MUST NOT retry. |
181: | ✅ **Verified** | High — confirmed by user | Root cause, correct fix, failed approaches. Primary reference. |
182: | ⏳ **Unverified** | Low — may be wrong | Agent's modifications awaiting user validation. Informational only. |
183: | ❌ **Failed**    | Negation of ⏳       | An ⏳ that failed a later check or got reimplemented badly. Same hard constraints as permissibility. |
184: 
185: **Core principle: unverified modifications are NOT facts. Never treat ⏳ entries as proven solutions.**

189: ## A7.6 On Every Skill Invocation — Memory Loading
190: 
191: When the skill triggers, load project memory in this order:
192: 
193: 1. **Check if `memory/MEMORY.md` exists**
194:    - YES → Read it (first 200 lines / 25KB automatically loaded via truncation)
195:    - NO → Check if old `MODIFY.html` exists. If yes, **migrate it** to the `memory/` directory structure (see A7.11). If neither exists, this is a fresh project — create `memory/MEMORY.md` with template from [MEMORY_TEMPLATES.md](MEMORY_TEMPLATES.md).
196: 
197: 2. **Scan the index** — For each section (User Context, Feedback, Project Context, External References, Fix Tracking), note the entries relevant to the current task.
198: 
199: 3. **Search before selecting** — Extract keywords from the user's request (problem symptom, feature name, file/module names, error messages). Use the `grep` tool to search `memory/*.md` for topic files whose names, descriptions, or bodies mention those keywords. This catches relevant memories whose index descriptions may not be obvious.
200: 
201: 4. **Select top 3-5 most relevant topic files** — Combine index scan + search results. Prioritize in this order:
202:    - ⛔ **Forbidden** entries touching the same area
203:    - ❌ **Failed** attempts with the same symptom
204:    - ✅ **Verified** fixes for the same files or problem
205:    - ⏳ **Unverified** attempts for the same problem
206:    - **Feedback** entries about the relevant approach or file
207:    Load only those files.
208: 
209: 5. **Verify references before trusting** — For any loaded memory that names specific files, functions, classes, configs, or line numbers, read the current code to confirm they still exist and mean the same thing. If a reference is stale, update or remove the memory entry and note the staleness.
210: 
211: 6. **Check for staleness** — For any loaded topic file with a `date` older than 14 days from today, display:
212:    ```
213:    > ⚠️ This memory is N days old. Memories are point-in-time observations — claims about code behavior or file:line citations may be outdated. Verify against current code before acting.
214:    ```
215: 
216: 7. **Check ⏳ Unverified entries** — If the user's current request overlaps an ⏳ fix entry in problem, symptom, affected file, or attempted solution, treat it as a failure signal. Mark that entry ❌ before attempting a new direction (see A7.7 Implicit Failure Detection).
217: 
218: 8. **✅ Verified staleness rule** — a ✅ entry is NOT immune to staleness; it only means it was verified at the commit recorded. When loading a ✅ fix entry:
219:    - If its `last_validated` is absent or >14 days old → mark it ⏳ again with a `stale: needs re-verification` note and re-verify before trusting.
220:    - If it has `file_refs[*].sha_at_time` and that ≠ current `git rev-parse HEAD:<path>` (or the ref is absent and the file moved) → same treatment: demote to ⏳ with a stale-refs note; re-verify code references against current code before acting on it.
221:    - A stale ✅ provides context but MUST NOT be relied on for downstream decisions until re-verified this session.
222:

225: ## A7.7 State Flow Rules (for fix-tracking entries)
226: 
227: ```
228: Agent modifies code
229:   ↓
230: Agent runs Playwright / automated tests
231:   ├─ Tests FAIL → create fix topic file with status ❌, try different direction
232:   └─ Tests PASS → create fix topic file with status ⏳ (NOT as ✅)
233:         ↓
234:   Next session begins:
235:     ├─ User gives same/similar prompt → auto-mark ⏳ as ❌, try different direction
236:     ├─ User explicitly says "still broken" → mark ⏳ as ❌, try different direction
237:     └─ User confirms "works" / no further complaint → promote to ✅ Verified
238: ```
239: 
240: **Implicit Failure Detection: if the user's current request overlaps an ⏳ fix entry in problem, symptom, affected file, or attempted solution, treat it as a failure signal. Mark that entry ❌ before attempting a new direction.**
241: 
242: **≥3 failures on same problem → escalate all failed methods to a ⛔ Forbidden topic file.**

246: ## A7.8 Pre-Change Guardrails
247: 
248: Before implementing any change:
249: 1. Check ⛔ **Forbidden** entries — do NOT use any listed method
250: 2. Scan ✅ **Verified** fix entries for files you are about to touch — learn from confirmed solutions
251: 3. Scan ⏳ **Unverified** fix entries for the current problem — if a pending entry exists, acknowledge it and explain why this attempt takes a different direction
252: 4. Check **Feedback** entries for relevant guidance on approach
253: 5. When touching a ⛔ flagged area, explicitly state why your approach avoids the forbidden pattern

257: ## A7.9 Post-Session Memory Writing ★ NON-NEGOTIABLE
258: 
259: **At the end of every session, before outputting the completion table, you MUST review and write memories:**
260: 
261: 1. **Review the conversation** — Identify new information worth persisting across sessions
262: 2. **Write topic files** for each new entry in `memory/` with proper frontmatter
263: 3. **Update MEMORY.md index** — Add pointer lines for new entries. Remove pointers to stale/removed entries
264: 4. **Fix-tracking rules:**
265:    - Write fix entries as `status: ⏳` if tests passed, `status: ❌` if tests failed
266:    - **Never write `status: ✅`** — only user confirmation can verify a fix
267:    - Include the commit short hash in the frontmatter (`commit: abc1234`) for every fix entry
268:    - Include **Failed Approaches** and **Rejected Alternatives** in fix topic bodies so future sessions do not rediscover the same dead ends
269:    - If ≥3 failures preceded this fix, create/update a ⛔ Forbidden entry
270: 5. **Record feedback memories** when user corrects or confirms approach during the session
271: 6. **Record project memories** when you learn about goals, deadlines, or team context
272: 7. **Check MEMORY.md caps** — If index exceeds 150 lines or 20KB, consolidate before adding more
273: 8. **Resolve the task working note** — distill `tests/working_note.md` (§A7.15) into the permanent topic files, then delete it (machine-checked by group 19 on the `--final` run)
274: 
275: **The checklist item "Memory topic file written to memory/" is MANDATORY for
276: any task that produced a lesson — lesson-triggered, not per-task ritual.**
277: Lesson-less tasks (Class DOC / trivial changes, §V11.3) state
278: `- memory: na (<why no lesson>)` in `tests/verification_log.md` instead of
279: writing filler topics (A7.1 "what NOT to save" — a forced empty topic is
280: worse than none).

284: ## A7.10 Final Memory Gate ★ NON-NEGOTIABLE
285: 
286: Before outputting the completion table, you MUST pass this gate. If any check fails, return to A7.9 and fix it before declaring the task complete.
287: 
288: 1. **Memory files exist** — At least one new or updated topic file exists in `memory/` for this session (unless the task was purely informational and produced nothing persistable).
289: 2. **Index updated** — `memory/MEMORY.md` contains a pointer to the new topic file(s), and the index is under 200 lines / 25KB.
290: 3. **Fix entries have commit** — Every `type: fix` topic file written this session includes `commit: <short-hash>` in its frontmatter. **History-rewrite waves (Class-E `git filter-repo`, ENGINEERING_STD §A10.1) must complete the commit-map hash remap BEFORE passing this gate** — every `commit:` cited in `memory/**` and `tests/verification_log.md` is rewritten from `.git/filter-repo/commit-map` (copy, never retype a hash), then this gate re-checks them.
291: 4. **No stale references introduced** — Any file/function/line cited in new memories was verified against current code during this session.
292: 5. **Scratchpad cleaned (legacy)** — the pre-§A7.15 `memory/.session-scratchpad.md` is superseded by tests/working_note.md; if a legacy scratchpad exists, delete it after permanent memories are written.
293: 6. **Working note resolved** — If `tests/working_note.md` was created (§A7.15), its persistable content was distilled into the topic files written this session and the file itself is deleted. The completion-time `assert_artifacts.py --final` run (group 19) machine-checks the deletion.
294: 
295: **Failure response:**
296: - If a memory should have been written but was not, write it now and re-run this gate.
297: - If you genuinely have nothing persistable (rare), explicitly state "No memory written — task was informational only" in the completion table's `What Changed` column.
298: 
299: **Explicit reporting:** In the line immediately before the completion table, output a single summary line:
300: ```
301: [Memory Gate] Passed: N new/updated topic file(s) | Index updated: yes/no | Commit hashes present: yes/no/N/A | Scratchpad cleaned: yes/no/N/A
302: ```
303: or, when nothing persistable was produced (§V11.3 lesson-triggered):
304: ```
305: [Memory Gate] na (<why no lesson>) — gate line field: memory_gate: na
306: ```
307: Do not output the completion table until this line is present and all answers are truthful.

311: ## A7.11 Promoting to Verified & Migration from Old Format
312: 
313: **Promoting a fix to ✅ Verified:**
314: When user confirms a fix works (or next session has no complaint about it):
315: 1. Change `status: ⏳` → `status: ✅` in the topic file's frontmatter
316: 2. Fill in **Root Cause**, **Failed Approaches**, and **Rejected Alternatives** in the body
317: 3. Add the verified commit short hash to the frontmatter (`commit: abc1234`)
318: 4. Add `file_refs` (path + range + `sha_at_time` from `git rev-parse <commit>:<path>`) for every file cited, and set `last_validated: <today>` — this makes the ✅ entry self-aging (A7.6 rule 8)
319: 5. Update the index line to show ✅ instead of ⏳
320: 6. If ≥3 failures preceded the fix, also create a ⛔ Forbidden entry
321: 
322: **Migrating from old MODIFY.html / MODIFY_COMPACT.html:**
323: If an old project has `MODIFY.html` or `MODIFY_COMPACT.html` but no `memory/` directory:
324: 1. Read the old file(s) completely
325: 2. Split each logical entry into a separate `memory/*.md` topic file with proper frontmatter
326: 3. Create `memory/MEMORY.md` with pointer lines for all entries

332: ## A7.12 Multi-Level Memory (User-Global + Project-Local)
333: 
334: **Two scopes are loaded and merged on session start:**
335: 
336: | Scope | Path | Content | Priority |
337: |-------|------|---------|----------|
338: | **User-global** | `~/.config/opencode/vibeweaver/memory/` | Cross-project user preferences, coding style, general feedback | Lower |
339: | **Project-local** | `<project>/memory/` | Project-specific architecture, fix tracking, team context | Higher |
340: 
341: **Loading order:** User-global MEMORY.md first → Project-local MEMORY.md second. If the same topic exists in both, project-local wins.
342: 
343: **What goes in user-global memory:**
344: - User's preferred languages, frameworks, and tools
345: - General coding conventions (e.g., "always use TypeScript strict mode")
346: - Feedback that applies across all projects (e.g., "never use `any` type")
347: - The user's role and expertise level
348: 
349: **What goes in project-local memory:**
350: - Everything else — fix tracking, project deadlines, project-specific conventions, external references
351: 
352: **On session start:** Read user-global MEMORY.md first, then project-local MEMORY.md. Select top 3-5 most relevant topic files combined across both scopes.
